'''Paul Jamaine''' "'''P. J.'''" '''Washington Jr.''' (born August 23, 1998) is an American college [[basketball]] player. He played for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]] of the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC).

==Early life==
Washington is the son of Sherry and Paul Washington Sr. He has two brothers Tyler and Spencer, and one sister Alexandria. Both of his parents played basketball at Middle Tennessee State. He wears number 25 because his father wore 25 in college.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/w/washington-pj.aspx|title=P.J. Washington|website=www.usab.com}}</ref>

===Recruiting===
Washington is considered as one of the best players in the 2017 recruiting class by [[Scout.com]], [[Rivals.com]] and [[ESPN]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Player/PJ-Washington-38650|title=P.J. Washington, Findlay Prep, Power Forward|website=247sports.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/187810/pj-washington|title=P.J. Washington - Basketball Recruiting - Player Profiles|publisher=ESPN}}</ref> On November 10, 2016 he committed to the Kentucky Wildcats, on November 20 he signed his letter of intent.

==College career==
Throughout most of his freshman season at Kentucky, Washington played through a pinkie injury that required surgery in the summer. In the NCAA Tournament loss to [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]], Washington led Kentucky with 18 points and 15 rebounds.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hale |first1=Jon |title=Can Reid Travis and PJ Washington play together in the same UK lineup? |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2018/08/08/kentucky-basketball-reid-travis-pj-washington-starting-lineups/911775002/ |accessdate=August 9, 2018 |work=[[Louisville Courier-Journal]] |date=August 8, 2018}}</ref> Washington averaged 10.8 points and 5.7 rebounds per game as a freshman. After the season, he declared for the NBA draft, but announced his return on May 30, 2018.<ref>{{cite news |title=PJ Washington will return as Kentucky's leading scorer; Wenyen Gabriel, Jarred Vanderbilt staying in draft |url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/23653768/pj-washington-returning-kentucky-wildcats-wenyen-gabriel-stay-nba-draft |accessdate=August 9, 2018 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=May 30, 2018}}</ref>

Following Kentucky's loss in the [[2019 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2019 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament]], Washington announced his intention to forgo his final two seasons of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2019 NBA Draft]], where projected to be a first-round selection.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/26477360/kentucky-washington-declares-nba-draft|title=Kentucky's Washington declares for NBA draft|work=[[ESPN]]|date=April 9, 2019}}</ref>
